header: I generate and embed the holiday policy chunks (see holiday-policy- chunk.model.ts) here, so free-text holiday policy questions become searchable: things structured queryHolidays() queries can never fully answer, like "can a new joiner get a full RH quota" or "what happens if my restricted holiday coincides with my weekly off". Two source types:
- "policyNote": a year-wide policy paragraph, embedded as-is (its own topic + text is already self-contained prose).

- "reclassification": one of holidayyear's own `note` values (why a specific holiday was promoted to an extra FH this year), embedded as a short synthesized sentence naming the holiday and date, so the chunk is self-contained even without its row's other context.

holidays/admin/store.ts calls this after a year's holidays/rhQuota are written. It is idempotent (it deletes then re-inserts this year's chunks), the same pattern as every other per-year sync in this codebase.

symbols.name: syncHolidayPolicyChunks
symbols.sig: export async function syncHolidayPolicyChunks( year: number, policyNotes: PolicyNoteInput[], reclassifications: ReclassificationInput[],): Promise<{ chunksWritten: number }>
doc: Rebuilds a year's holiday policy chunks from scratch: the policyNotes array (as given in the enriched upload JSON) plus every holiday that carries a non-null `note` (already persisted on holidayyear rows by the time this runs). I delete this year's existing chunks first, so re-running (e.g. re-uploading a corrected file) never duplicates.

symbols.name: buildPolicyChunkRows
symbols.sig: export async function buildPolicyChunkRows( year: number, policyNotes: PolicyNoteInput[], reclassifications: ReclassificationInput[],): Promise<PolicyChunkRow[]>

symbols.name: writePolicyChunkRows
symbols.sig: export async function writePolicyChunkRows( q: (sql: string, params?: unknown[]) => Promise<any[]>, year: number, rows: PolicyChunkRow[],): Promise<number>
doc: Replaces the year's policy chunks with these rows, on the caller's connection (inside its transaction).
